commands.review_summary:
This PR hardens exe.dev reuse and deletion around canonical ownership tags, unchanged local claims, deterministic VM names, and provider-supported inventory, with matching docs and regression tests.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main flows raw exe.dev VM-name or SSH-host resolution into `deleteVM`, and the PR-head endpoint gap is visible by persisting a claim and then changing the inventory `ssh_dest` before release.

target.title: fix: bind exe.dev deletion to exact claims
target.body:
## Summary

- require a complete canonical exe.dev ownership tag set plus an exact local provider/resource claim before reuse or deletion
- bind claims to the deterministic VM name, SSH endpoint, and approved exe.dev control route
- re-read inventory and verify the unchanged claim while holding the claim lock across deletion; retain claims after failures
- keep claimless or incomplete resources read-only, with conflict-safe explicit adoption for fully tagged VMs
- use the provider-supported `ls --l --json` inventory call instead of the invalid `--a` flag

Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/926

## Verification

- `go test -race ./internal/providers/exedev`
- `go build -trimpath -o /tmp/crabbox-exedev-926-full ./cmd/crabbox`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `npm run format:check --prefix worker`
- `npm run lint --prefix worker`
- `npm run check --prefix worker`
- `npm test --prefix worker` (866 passed, 3 skipped)
- `npm run build --prefix worker`
- `node scripts/build-docs-site.mjs`
- AutoReview local and branch modes: no accepted/actionable findings

## Live proof

- Authenticated `ssh exe.dev whoami --json` succeeds.
- Authenticated `ssh exe.dev ls --l --json` succeeds and reports zero VMs.
- Candidate `crabbox list --provider exe-dev --all --json` succeeds and reports zero VMs.
- The attempted create reached exe.dev but was rejected before resource creation because the account has no active plan. No remote VM or local claim residue exists.

Merge remains gated on an authenticated create/use/deny/destroy zero-residue canary on this exact candidate, or an explicit item-specific waiver.
